newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends sharply up,heating oil still driver. [CORRECTED 20:14 GMT]
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends sharply up,heating oil still driver. [CORRECTED 20:14 GMT]

text.p: IPE Brent made a concerted late dash to session highs as support levels were sucessfully tested, resistance targets passed and traders short-covered.

IPE November Brent last traded at $23.43 per barrel (corrects from tonne) up 54 cents (corrects from 50), having touched $23.49 minutes before the close. Brent's late bull run was attributed to it having sucessfully tested support of $22.65 per barrel (corrects from tonne) with a low of $22.67 and passed, albeit in thinnish volume, a resistance level of $23.40 per barrel (corrects from tonne).
"We have seen acceptance of the higher levels and people are covering themselves," said one IPE trader.
Traders said $23.40 would continue to be an important level on Monday. "We didn't breach it with enough volume today. It ($23.40) should still stand.
The energy complex driver remained buoyant NYMEX heating oil.
"Everyone is looking to the U.S. and jumping in," said a dealer.
NYMEX October heating oil last traded at 71.50 cents a gallon, up .60 cents with dealers saying most volume was seen at the higher end.

"Some people are looking for Thursday's high of $72.80, but I think that's pegged a bit high," said one dealer. Heating oil continues to be supported by low stocks in the U.S. and Europe and the approach of colder weather.
IPE gas oil ended the day lower after profit taking knocked off some of yesterday's gains.
October gas oil ended down $3.25 a tonne at $228.75, but traders felt there remained room next week for further rises.
